subject: Novabridge live feed: intermittent chunk drops & elevated error rate — escalation

From: Luke Tanner <luke@novabridge.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: support@novabridge.com
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime feed cutting out — streaming chunks stop, error rate rising

Irene,

We started seeing steady client errors on our production chat flows starting ~08:50 PDT. Users report long pauses (~8–12s) followed by partial responses or nothing; our observability shows a spike in 502/504 responses and a lot of WS closes with code 1006. Token throughput also dropped ~30% from baseline.

Attached are the snippet logs and a dump of the last failing websocket session (novabridge-ws-close-1006.log and partial-frame-dump-20280402.txt). We need confirmation this isn’t on our side — can you triage? This is impacting a handful of power users and we’re seeing churn risk.

Luke Tanner
Senior Platform Engineer
Novabridge

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Cc: Luke Tanner <luke@novabridge.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Realtime feed cutting out — streaming chunks stop, error rate rising

Irene/Dylan/Tessa — I looked at the customer traces and host metrics for the timeframe Luke reported. Summary:
- Multiple connections from Novabridge are hitting proxy timeout and being re-routed to a lower-priority pool briefly; during the re-route we see chunked transfers drop mid-stream (client sees silence then abrupt close).
- The initial failures correlate with a brief surge of long-running decode requests on node gpu-12 (seq-len outlier). Kernel saturation caused tail latency spikes and our routing decision sent some traffic to the cold pool where keepalive thresholds differ.
- I opened INF-7192 to collect a full stack trace and pinned the affected instances.

Immediate remediation proposed (can do within 20–30m):
1) Temporarily pin Novabridge traffic to dedicated pool A (avoid cold pool fallback).
2) Reduce per-request max_seq_len to trim outlier requests (ask Novabridge to cap long inputs) — low-confidence but quick.
3) Roll a micro-patch to align keepalive/heartbeat thresholds between pools (requires safe restart of 2/8 machines in pool).

Triage notes attached. I recommend we escalate to Marcus for exec-level signoff on reserve capacity pinning while we stabilize.

—Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Luke Tanner <luke@novabridge.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Realtime feed cutting out — streaming chunks stop, error rate rising

Quick technical summary:
- Observed repeated WS close code 1006 with server-side trace indicating a forced connection drop when the kernel queue exceeded 95% for >3s.
- Chunked transfer frames were partial (final bit not set) in ~12% of sampled fails — suggests our output coalescer occasionally fails to flush frames when preempted by urgent batched jobs.
- Correlating job queue with autoscale logs: a background quantization job triggered at 08:43 which briefly increased GPU memory pressure across pool A.

I support Marissa’s remediation plan. Additional ask to the customer: provide 3 example request IDs and timestamps in the next 10 minutes so we can cross-link traces and do a deterministic replay.

Dylan Brooks
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Customer impact: elevated error rates (502/504), WS close 1006, ~30% throughput drop for affected sessions.
- Root cause drivers: short window of GPU kernel saturation + autoscaler routing to a cold pool with stricter keepalive thresholds.
- Proposed immediate actions: pin Novabridge traffic to dedicated pool A (estimated cost delta $2.5k/day), apply keepalive threshold alignment patch (requires safe restart of 2/8 machines — <10m per machine), ask customer to temporarily cap input lengths.

Request: Marcus — please sign off on emergency reserve pin for up to 24 hours while we stabilize; if we get sign-off I will inform Luke and execute steps 1 & 3 immediately.

—Irene

Luke — quick update and next steps.

What we did (completed 12:30 PDT):
- Pinned Novabridge traffic to dedicated pool A for 24 hours to avoid cold-pool fallback.
- Rolled the keepalive/heartbeat alignment micro-patch (2 machines restarted safely).
- Increased monitoring window and enabled aggressive tracing for Novabridge request_ids you provided.

Immediate customer ask: please limit per-request sequence length to <= 4k tokens until we complete INF-7192 analysis (estimated 48 hours).

Observed effect (post-change): error rates dropped to near-baseline within ~15 minutes, and WS close 1006 events ceased for the sampled sessions. We still want to complete the causal analysis (INF-7192) and propose a longer-term fix for autoscaler preemption and coalescer flush behavior.

I’ll follow up with a post-mortem and timeline within 48 hours. Let me know if you want a short sync with Marcus on the cost tradeoff.
